newsitem.title: USA: Interface Systems audits U.K. operation.
newsitem.headline: Interface Systems audits U.K. operation.

text.p: Interface Systems Inc said Friday it was auditing the balance sheet of its U.K. distribution business after a downturn in the business and the discovery of accounting errors.
Interface said Thursday it lost $6.9 million or $1.57 a share in the third quarter ended June 30 compared to a loss of $1.5 million or $O.33 in the same period last year.
This year's results included charges of $6.1 million related to a downturn in the UK distribution business, inventory adjustments in the UK and a write-off of capitalized software development costs.

The loss was centered on the company's distribution business in the U.K., it said. Results for the quarter were negatively impacted by a downturn in sales at the operation due to a decline in market conditions and continued product price erosion, Robert Nero, president and chief executive, said in a statement.

Duing the quarter the company wrote off $1.1 million resulting from several accounting errors related to inventory at its U.K. business. As a result of the errors, an audit by Arthur Andersen Llp is underway of the June 30, 1997 balance sheet of the distribution business.
The audit so far has resulted in additional adjustments of $800,000 that were recorded during the quarter, the company said.

In addition, Ken Sinden, managing director of the U.K. operation since inception, has resigned. The business has been restructured to consist of two separate units, distribution and core, to focus each unit on its respective market and on a return to profitability. Separate managing directors have been appointed to run the new operating units. The combined workforce in the United Kingdom has been reduced by 15 employees, or about 18 percent. The reductions were made in July and expenses will be taken in the fourth quarter.

Based on an evaluation of future market conditions, Interface wrote-off $1.5 million of goodwill during the quarter related to its investment in the U.K. operations and recorded a reserve of $1.4 million for slow-moving inventory and fair market value reductions, it said.
